doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Bass players he went to hear: Slam Stewart and others
summary: He recalls Slam Stewart with Illinois Jacquet, Milt Hinton, Duvivier and Mraz.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: So who were the other bass players around New York at that time that you would go out of your way to go see?

To go see? Slam Stewart. One of my favorite nights of jazz I ever heard was Slam with Illinois Jacquet. It was a quartet setting at the Village Vanguard. And he didn’t use any amp and he had gut strings on an old Kay bass with a little ribbon microphone out front. Sounded great. That was one of my favorite experiences. That and anywhere Milt Hinton was of course, Duvivier was still playing, George Mraz was on the scene and I used to go see him, I saw him with Zoot a couple of times. Basically though if you’re a musician you don’t get a whole lot of chances, you don’t get enough chance to go out and hear the people that you’d like to. Because usually they’re working the same night you are. I never run into bass players. I run into everybody else. On a festival like this I’ll run into two other bass players. But in a normal day to day gigging situation, you hardly ever run into any. And drummers, same thing, because there’s only one per gig.
